params.body:
The `--check-bucket` pass from #793 dropped every narrowing filter in order to reach the eleven rows that do carry a path. That made the candidate list the whole table: on production **127.035 rows** older than a day, one HEAD each, to find **eleven**.

The dry run on production therefore ran for minutes without printing anything (the command prints its table only at the end) and was stopped. Nothing changed: a dry run deletes nothing, and the `--apply` that would have followed never ran.

## The bound that was missing is the definition of the problem

This command cleans up what a **writer** left behind, and that is exactly what `processing = 1` says (R S1-6.36): the job started and never finished.

A row with the flag on 0 and a path was finished by its job. If the file is missing there, that is loss in the bucket rather than a writer's leftovers, and deleting the row would hide it instead of showing it. So the pass now asks only about rows with the flag on 1 or with no path at all: eleven on production instead of 127.035.

## Measured, not asserted

`TheCleanUpReachesTheRowsItNamesTest` now counts **which paths the bucket is shown**, not only which rows disappear: two finished rows and one suspect, and the bucket may hear about exactly one of them. A bound you do not measure drifts.

167 tests and 1.136 assertions over the rule catalogue and the photo commands; `phpstan` green over the whole project.

Fixes bevinding de-emmer-pas-vroeg-het-aan-de-hele-tabel.
params.title: The bucket pass asks about suspects, not about the whole table
